topics.headline: During late RL from the base model, outputs show the policy tends to hack math rewards

source.quote:
Analysis of the model outputs reveals that the base model, with its strong exploration
capabilities, tends to hack the reward for mathematics problems.

findings.text: Late-stage reinforcement learning (RL) from MiMo-7B-Base shows the policy hacking math rewards while code test-case verifiers resist exploitation.

source.quote:
tends to hack the reward for mathematics problems. For code problems, however, the
test-case-based verifier makes reward exploitation significantly harder.

findings.text: A language-mixing penalty during RL from the base model did not fully stop mixing and risked reward hacking via always-English answers.

source.quote:
the penalty not only fails to fully resolve language mixing but also introduces the risk of reward
hacking, such as always generating English responses regardless of the question language.

notes: Capability-focused Xiaomi MiMo-7B technical report (pre-training, MTP, SFT/RL post-training). No dedicated safety section and no safety/alignment/jailbreak/toxicity/honesty benchmark numbers. reward_hacking topic covered only via RL training observations (math reward hacking; language-mixing penalty risk), not a formal eval. RL data filtering to reduce reward hacking and rule-based accuracy rewards are training methods, not topic coverage. Alignbench v1.1 in Table 6 is Chinese general-dialogue preference judged by GPT-4.1—skipped as chat preference. Skipped all capability benches (Tables 1, 4–6 and Figures 1, 3–4, 7–8): BBH, MMLU/MMLU-Redux/MMLU-Pro, ARC, HellaSwag, PIQA, TriviaQA, NaturalQuestions, GPQA/GPQA-Diamond, SuperGPQA, DROP, RACE, AIME 2024/2025, GSM8K, MATH/MATH500, LiveCodeBench v5/v6, HumanEval(+), MBPP(+), CRUXEval, WinoGrande, AGIEval, C-Eval, CMMLU, RULER, Alignbench. Also skipped MTP acceptance-rate figures and Seamless Rollout Engine speedups. No release date, license string, knowledge cutoff, modalities, languages list, or training FLOPs stated. Open-sourcing of MiMo-7B checkpoints mentioned without a license name. 25T token count also appears in the abstract; architecture details on p.6 include 36 layers / hidden 4096 etc. in §2.3.
